title: Southwest monsoon advances further into eastern, southern India, heavy rains forecast for northeast - DD News
article_text:
The Southwest monsoon has made significant progress, advancing into the remaining parts of Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, and the west-central Bay of Bengal, along with additional areas of Telangana, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Bihar on Monday, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The northern limit of the Monsoon currently passes through Harnai, Solapur, Hyderabad, Bhadrachalam, Koraput, Phulbani, Ranchi, Jamui, and Muzaffarpur.

Conditions remain favourable for further advancement into parts of the central Arabian Sea, Maharashtra, the remaining regions of Karnataka, Telangana, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, and some areas of Chhattisgarh over the next 4-5 days, the IMD said.

In the past 24 hours, the monsoon brought substantial relief and activity. Heavy to very heavy rainfall (12-20 cm) was recorded at isolated places in Assam, with heavy rainfall (7-11 cm) in coastal Karnataka, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, and parts of Tamil Nadu.

Thunderstorms accompanied by squally winds reaching 60-100 kmph lashed several regions, including east Rajasthan, Telangana, Odisha, and west Madhya Pradesh.

Looking ahead, the IMD has issued warnings for isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall over sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Meghalaya during the next 6-7 days. Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall is expected across the Northeast, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, sub-Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim, and Kerala. Isolated heavy rainfall is also likely in parts of Bihar, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu, with very heavy spells possible in the Northeast later in the week.

Several weather systems are influencing the pattern. A seasonal trough runs from Punjab to Bihar, while upper air cyclonic circulations persist over south central Maharashtra and south Punjab. A western disturbance over north Pakistan is expected to affect northwest India from June 18, bringing more rain and possible hail over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh and adjoining areas. In contrast, heat wave conditions are very likely in isolated pockets over Telangana (June 15-16) and Vidarbha (June 15-17). Hot and humid weather will prevail over Konkan & Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, and Odisha. Warm night conditions are also expected in parts of Konkan and Goa.

Meanwhile, the highest maximum temperature of 42.8 degrees Celsius was reported in Rajasthan’s Phalodi.

For Delhi, NCR, a spell of very light to light rain with thunderstorms and strong winds (50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph) was likely on Monday, with maximum temperatures around 35-37 degrees Celsius. Winds will remain gusty over the next few days amid partly to generally cloudy skies.

In an advisory, the IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into vulnerable sea areas in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea until June 20. Farmers in rain-affected regions have been urged to ensure proper drainage and secure standing crops, while the public is cautioned against thunderstorm hazards, including lightning and strong winds. Citizens in heat-prone areas should stay hydrated and avoid prolonged sun exposure.

–IANS

नई दिल्ली

उत्तर भारत में कुछ समय के मॉनसूनी ब्रेक के बाद एक बार फिर बारिश का सिलसिला शुरू हो गया है। मौसम विभाग (IMD) के मुताबिक, उत्तर, पूर्वोत्तर और पश्चिमी भारत के राज्यों में 7 अगस्त तक भारी बारिश का दौर जारी रहेगा। इसके अलावा दक्षिण प्रायद्वीपीय भारत में बारिश कम होगी। अगले पांच दिनों तक कई राज्यों में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। 3 अगस्त से 7 या 8 अगस्त तक पहाड़ों में भी भारी बारिश का दौर जारी रहेगा। ऐसे में पर्यटकों को सावधान रहने की सलाह दी गई है।

16 राज्यों में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट
मौसम विभाग ने उत्तर प्रदेश, बिहार, झारखंड, पश्चिम बंगाल, असम, मेघायलट, त्रिपुरा, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, मिजोरम, दिल्ली, पंजाब, हरियाणा, राजस्थान, ओडिशा, सिक्किम, मणिपुर और मध्य प्रेदश में मध्यम से भारी बारिश की संभावना जताई है। इसके अलावा ज्यादातर राज्यों में 30 से 50 किलोमीटर प्रतिघंटा की रफ्तार से हवाएं चल सकती हैं। पहाड़ी राज्यों में भूस्खलन का भी अलर्ट जारी किया गया है।

यूपी-बिहार का मौसम
मौसम विभाग ने 3 से 8 अगस्त तक पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया है। बारिश का दौर पूरे रराज्यमें ही जारी रहेगा। मौसम विभाग ने कहा है कि 3 अगस्त को लखनऊ, उन्नाव, सीतापुर, बहराइच, बाराबंकी, गोंडा, रायबरेली, प्रयागराज, वाराणसी, मिर्जापुर, सोनभद्र, चंदौली, देविरिया, बलिया, सिद्धार्थनगर, कुशीनगर, संत कबीरनगर, आंबेडकर नगर, अयोध्या, बस्ती और अन्य पूर्वी जिलों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश हो सकती है।

मौसम विभाग ने बिहार में भी 3 अगस्त को भारी बारिश की संभावना जताी है। यहां अधिकतर जिले में 3 से 5 अगस्त तक बारिश का दौर जारी रहगा। इसके अलावा हवाओं की रफ्तार 40 से 50 किलोमीटर प्रतिघंटा की रह सकती है।

दिल्ली में हो सकती बारिश
मौसम विभाग ने दिल्ली में 4 से 7 अगस्त तक मध्यम से भारी बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया है। वहीं 3 अगस्त को हल्की बारिश हो सकती है। राजधानी का अधिकतम तापमान 33 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 25 डिग्री रह सकता है। वहीं दिल्ली एनसीआर में बादल छाए रहेंगे।

पहाड़ों में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट
मौसम विभाग ने हिमाचल प्रदेश में 3 से 8 अगस्त तक कई जिलों में बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया है। इसमें चंबा, हमीरपुर, किन्नौर, कांगड़ा, लाहौल, कुल्लू, मंडी, सिरमौर, शिमला और सोलन जिले शामिल हैं। वहीं उत्तराखंड के बागेश्वर, चमोली, देहरादून, उत्तर काशी, रूद्रप्रयाग जिलों में बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। जम्मू-कश्मीर में बारिश से बुरा हाल है। मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक अगले चार दिनों तक जम्मू-कश्मीर में भारी बारिश जारी रहेगी। कश्मीर में कहीं पहाड़ दड़क रहे हैं तो कहीं बादल फट रहे हैं। ऐसे में अनंतनाग, कुलगाम, बारामूला समेत कई जिलों में अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। कश्मीर की नदियां उफान पर हैं और जन-जीवन अस्तव्यस्त हो गया है।

पंजाब और हरियाणा का मौसम
मौसम विभाग ने पंजाब और हरियाणा में भी 3 और 4 अगस्त को व्यापक बारिश की संभावना जताई है। इसके बाद 5 और 6 तारीख को भी अलग-अलग जगहों पर बारिश का सिलसिला जारी रहेगा। वहीं 8 अगस्त को हल्की बारिश हो सकती है। साथ ही राजस्थान में भी 3 से 8 अगस्त तक बारिश का दौर जारी रहेगा। हवा की गति 30 से 40 किलोमीटर प्रतिघंटा रह सकती है।

रांची। देश के कई हिस्सों में मानसून एक बार फिर सक्रिय हो गया है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) ने हरियाणा, पंजाब, दिल्ली, उत्तर प्रदेश, मध्य प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़, बिहार और झारखंड समेत कई राज्यों में अगले कुछ दिनों तक भारी बारिश, तेज हवाओं और वज्रपात की संभावना जताई है।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, 3 से 6 अगस्त के दौरान हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़, दिल्ली और पंजाब के कई इलाकों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है। वहीं, पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में 3 से 7 अगस्त और पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में 4 से 7 अगस्त तक अच्छी बारिश का दौर जारी रहने की संभावना है। इतिहास

मध्य प्रदेश और छत्तीसगढ़ में भारी बारिश

आईएमडी के मुताबिक, 3 से 6 अगस्त तक पश्चिमी मध्य प्रदेश, 3 अगस्त को पूर्वी मध्य प्रदेश और 3 से 5 अगस्त तक विदर्भ के कुछ हिस्सों में बारिश हो सकती है। वहीं 7 और 8 अगस्त को पश्चिमी मध्य प्रदेश तथा 3 से 8 अगस्त के बीच छत्तीसगढ़ के कई क्षेत्रों में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश होने की संभावना है।

बिहार में इन जिलों में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट

3 अगस्त को सीतामढ़ी, मधुबनी, दरभंगा, सुपौल, अररिया, किशनगंज, पूर्णिया, कटिहार, सहरसा, मधेपुरा, मुजफ्फरपुर, वैशाली और समस्तीपुर सहित उत्तर एवं पूर्वोत्तर बिहार के कई जिलों में भारी बारिश की संभावना है।

वहीं पटना, गया, भागलपुर, मुंगेर, बेगूसराय, खगड़िया, नालंदा, नवादा, जमुई और पश्चिम चंपारण सहित दक्षिण और मध्य बिहार के कई जिलों में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश के आसार हैं।

झारखंड में बारिश, तेज हवा और वज्रपात की चेतावनी

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, 3 अगस्त को झारखंड के कई हिस्सों में बारिश हो सकती है। इस दौरान 40 से 50 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चलने और वज्रपात की भी आशंका है।

इसके अलावा 4 अगस्त को गिरिडीह, देवघर, जामताड़ा, धनबाद और बोकारो जिलों में एक-दो स्थानों पर भारी बारिश हो सकती है।

दिल्ली में बादल और बारिश के आसार

राष्ट्रीय राजधानी दिल्ली में 3 अगस्त को दिनभर बादल छाए रहने और हल्की बारिश की संभावना है। वहीं 4 अगस्त को मध्यम बारिश के साथ कुछ क्षेत्रों में गरज-चमक और तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं।

राजस्थान में कई इलाकों में घटेगी बारिश

राजस्थान में 3 अगस्त से मानसून ट्रफ उत्तर की ओर खिसकने के कारण जोधपुर, उदयपुर, कोटा और भरतपुर संभाग में बारिश की गतिविधियों में कमी आने की संभावना है।

हालांकि 3 से 5 अगस्त के दौरान बीकानेर संभाग, शेखावाटी, जयपुर और भरतपुर संभाग के कुछ हिस्सों में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश हो सकती है। राज्य के अन्य क्षेत्रों में मौसम मुख्यतः शुष्क रहने का अनुमान है।

मौसम विभाग ने लोगों से खराब मौसम के दौरान सतर्क रहने, वज्रपात के समय खुले स्थानों में न जाने और स्थानीय प्रशासन द्वारा जारी एडवाइजरी का पालन करने की अपील की है।

Monsoon fury grips India: 15 dead in Kerala, Karnataka grapples with flooding, landslides
Torrential rains trigger landslides, school closures, and mass evacuations in Kerala; coastal Karnataka faces swollen rivers and blocked highways
The Federal
3 Aug 2026 9:36 AM  (Updated:3 Aug 2026 1:10 PM)
Click the Play button to hear this message in audio format

Kerala and coastal Karnataka continue to reel under severe monsoon even as the flood situation in Assam eases slightly.

As many as 15 people have died while seven remain missing in Kerala, Chief Minister VD Satheesan said.

Several parts of the state recorded heavy rainfall, with three weather stations receiving more than 100 mm of rain, according to IMD data released on Monday (August 3), as authorities warned of a worsening situation in the southern district of Pathanamthitta.

The office of Kerala Tourism Minister PC Vishnunadh said heavy rain in the Sabarimala region had created a worrying situation in the district, with water levels likely to rise in Ranni and nearby areas.

Also read: Flood here, drought there: A tale of two Indias in monsoon

Vishnunadh is camping in Pathanamthitta and leading disaster management and relief operations, the minister's office said. It added that he was reviewing the situation at Kozhencherry along with Aranmula MLA Abin Varkey, government officials and other elected representatives.

Dams reach red alert levels

Meanwhile, one shutter of the Moozhiyar reservoir in the district was opened by 15 cms as its water level reached red alert status, officials said.

They advised people living on the banks of Kakkattar and Pampa rivers to be cautious.

Besides Moozhiyar, other major power generation dams, like Kallarkutty, Erattayar and Lower Periyar in Idukki, Poringalkuthu in Thrissur and Kuttiyadi in Kozhikode also have water levels in the red alert status, they said.

The rains also caused a landslide at a construction site at Panakkad in Malappuram, which was reportedly close to the residence of state Industries Minister P K Kunhalikutty.

Recue ops underway

While the landslide did not cause any loss of life, it led to the blocking of traffic on the main road along the construction site.

From Kollam, fishing boats were being transported by road to Aranmula in Pathanamthitta, which is flooded, to help in rescue efforts, according to visuals on TV channels.

People living in low-lying areas have been directed to move to safer places without fail, as heavy rain overnight raised concerns of flooding in vulnerable areas.

Schools shut down

In view of the continuing heavy rainfall in Kerala, collectors of many districts have declared a holiday on Monday for all educational institutions.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Satheesan has convened an online meeting of district collectors at 10 am to review the rain situation across Kerala.

According to the India Meteorological Department, rainfall data recorded between 8.30 am on August 2 and 5.30 am on August 3 showed that Venkurinji in Pathanamthitta received the highest rainfall at 104.5 mm, followed by Udumbannoor in Idukki with 103.0 mm and Cheruthoni in Idukki with 101.5 mm.

Laha in Pathanamthitta received 87.0 mm of rain, while Thycattussery in Alappuzha recorded 80.0 mm. Neriamangalam in Ernakulam received 75.0 mm, followed by Ulanadu in Pathanamthitta with 74.5 mm.

Mattancherry in Ernakulam recorded 71.0 mm of rainfall. Ranni Chethackal in Pathanamthitta received 65.5 mm, Vadavathoor in Kottayam recorded 64.0 mm, Palluruthy in Ernakulam received 63.0 mm, and Munakkal in Thrissur recorded 62.0 mm.

According to the IMD, all these places recorded 60 mm or more of rainfall during the period, which the weather office classifies as significant rainfall.

Rescue operation underway after three members of a family, including a three-year-old child, were killed after a rain-triggered landslide buried their shed at Indiranagar, in Shivamogga district, Karnataka, Sunday, August 2. PTI Photo

Coastal Karnataka battered

In Karnataka, which has been reeling under drought-like conditions, torrential monsoon rains and strong winds battered the coastal Dakshina Kannada district overnight on Saturday-Sunday, triggering landslides, inundating roads and low-lying areas, and swelling major rivers.

The district administration placed emergency response mechanisms, including the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), on high alert as several rivers rose to dangerous levels after relentless downpours across Western Ghats catchment areas.

The Netravathi, Kumaradhara, Mrutyunjaya, Phalguni (Gurupura), and Somavathi rivers were reported flowing near or above danger marks, threatening riverside settlements and agricultural belts. Water levels have risen rapidly; downstream communities are being monitored and alerted.

Roads blocked, low-lying areas submerged

Landslides and flash floods blocked key routes and disrupted connectivity across the district. In Belthangady taluk, landslides obstructed the Mundaje-Dharmasthala route, while flash currents caused a retaining wall to collapse at Neriya, inundating nearby residential pockets.

Also read: Assam flood leaves 78 dead; IMD predicts more rains till August 3

Low-lying areca nut plantations, agricultural fields, and houses in Mundaje and Ujire were submerged. Authorities warned citizens, tourists, and pilgrims against approaching riverbanks, waterlogged roads, and beaches. Fishermen were ordered to stay ashore owing to surface winds and high waves.

Heavy earth-moving equipment was deployed on national highway corridors, including Charmadi, Shiradi, and Sampaje Ghat routes, to clear potential landslide debris and maintain movement for essential services.

Volunteers carry relief kits to flood-affected families at a temporary shelter, in Upper Assam. Handout via PTI Photo

Assam flood eases

In better news, the flood situation in Assam improved on Sunday, with around 1.35 lakh people now affected in five districts even though three more persons died, taking the toll in this year’s deluge to 85, according to an official bulletin.

All three deaths were reported from Sivasagar district.

The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) reported that more than 1,36,200 people have been affected by floods in the Charaideo, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, and Sivasagar districts. On Saturday, almost 1.8 lakh people were affected across five districts.

Also read: Monsoon mayhem: Floods ravage Kerala, Odisha, Assam; IMD warns of more rain

Sivasagar is the worst-hit district with over 55,000 people affected, followed by 40,000 people in Charaideo and 22,000 in Jorhat. According to ASDMA, 335 villages are inundated, while 15,422 hectares of farmland have been damaged.

The administration has been operating 54 relief camps and relief distribution centres in five districts, taking care of 13,771 people at present. At present, the Dhansiri river is flowing above the danger level at Numaligarh.

The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority placed 12 districts under an orange rainfall alert at 13:00 LT on August 2. The alerts covered Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod.

Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam were under yellow alerts. An orange alert corresponds to isolated rainfall of 115 to 205 mm (4.6 to 8 inches) in 24 hours, while a yellow alert covers rainfall of 65 to 115 mm (2.5 to 4.5 inches).

The India Meteorological Department recorded 250 mm (9.8 inches) of rain at Laha in Pathanamthitta during the 24 hours ending at 08:30 LT on August 1. Its national bulletin was issued at 13:30 LT the same day.

An offshore trough extended from southern Gujarat to Kerala at mean sea level. IMD forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Kerala and Mahe on August 1, followed by isolated very heavy rainfall on August 2.

IMD also forecast thunderstorms, lightning and winds of 40–50 km/h (25–31 mph), with gusts reaching 60 km/h (37 mph), across Kerala and Mahe. Fishermen were advised not to enter affected waters off the Kerala coast.

The Kerala Government warned that intense rainfall over short periods could cause flash floods, mountain runoff and waterlogging in urban and low-lying areas. Prolonged rainfall also raised the risk of landslides and mudslides in vulnerable terrain.

KSDMA instructed people in landslide-prone locations, beside rivers and downstream from dams to move to safer areas when directed. Residents were advised not to cross rivers, enter water bodies or drive through flooded road sections.

The authority advised the public to avoid waterfalls, mountainous areas and nonessential travel while rainfall warnings remained active. Taluk and district control rooms were operating around the clock, with emergency assistance available through the toll-free numbers 1077 and 1070.

Yellow alerts were listed for 10 districts on August 3. KSDMA said district warning levels could be revised as IMD issued updated rainfall forecasts.

August falls within South Asia’s monsoon season, when flooding commonly intensifies across monsoon-affected regions. The confirmed deaths, missing people, injuries, displacement and housing damage raised the event to a major operational-impact level.

title: Tourist Killed at Restricted Kerala Waterfall While Monsoon Ban Was in Force - Travelers Today
article_text:
A general view shows the Cheruthoni Dam with its shutters open after water levels reached a height 2395 ft. following torrential rains in south India state of Kerala, in Idukki on October 19, 2021. - Forecasters have also warned of more heavy rains in the coming days in the southern state of Kerala where floods have already killed at least 27 people since October 15. APPU S. NARAYANAN/GETTY IMAGES

A woman from Coimbatore died and a companion was rescued Sunday after their five-person group entered the Palakkuzhi waterfall in Palakkad, Kerala — a site that the district administration had formally banned to tourists because of monsoon-driven flash-flood conditions — and police have opened an investigation into how the group bypassed the restriction with no physical checkpoint blocking their path.

Bhanupriya, 40, a resident of Coimbatore, was swept downstream and fell onto a rocky stretch of the falls in Kizhakkencherry, Palakkad district. After approximately two hours of attempts using rope rescue equipment, fire service personnel found her dead. Her companion, Bharath, 35, who works at an IT park in Coimbatore, was pulled to safety from roughly 60 feet below the falls by a Palakkad fire services rope rescue team after he fell onto rocks and sustained minor injuries. He was shifted to hospital for treatment. The remaining three members of the group were not reported to have entered the water.

A Formal Ban Was Active Before the Group Left Coimbatore

The Palakkad district administration had prohibited visitors from all hilly areas in the district — explicitly including waterfalls — because of heavy monsoon rainfall and the elevated risk of flash floods and landslides, according to officials cited by PTI. That restriction was in place by August 1, 2026, the day before the group traveled. On the same day, the Kerala Tourism Department advisory and the District Tourism Promotion Council issued a statewide notice making clear that all waterfalls, reservoirs, and water-based tourist destinations in districts under Red or Orange alerts would remain closed until weather warnings were withdrawn. Palakkad was specifically listed as an Orange Alert district, meaning very heavy rainfall of between 115.6 and 204.4 millimeters within 24 hours was expected.

Officials at the Vadakkencherry fire station said they received the alert at 12:40 PM IST. One unit each from Vadakkencherry, Alathur, and Palakkad reached the site along with a special rope rescue team from Palakkad. A fire services official told Onmanorama that the waterfall "had strong currents due to heavy rainfall over the past two days," and added that "several tourists had reached the location" despite the ban — indicating the group was not the only one to enter the restricted area that day.

Police Are Investigating How Five Tourists Entered a Closed Waterfall Area

The central question for authorities is how a group traveling from another state was able to reach the waterfall at all. Police said the group arrived from Coimbatore unaware of the restrictions, but the investigation is focused specifically on what, if anything, was physically in place to stop them. No checkpoint, barrier, or ranger was reported at the scene; the investigation into how the group bypassed the restriction implicitly confirms that enforcement was absent on the ground.

According to the Kerala Tourism Department's August 1 advisory, officials and the Motor Vehicles Department were directed to conduct "strict inspections at check posts and key roads" in hilly districts, and the District Tourism Promotion Council and Forest Department were told to ensure tourists received proper safety warnings. Whether those instructions were carried out at the access road to Palakkuzhi — which fire services described as "deep inside a forest area" — is part of the open investigation. India's prohibitory orders are now issued under Section 163 of the BNSS, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which replaced the older Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, meaning violations now carry the risk of detention and prosecution rather than simple fines. Whether the group or the site's access route will face legal scrutiny under those provisions has not yet been determined.

Which Kerala Waterfalls and Hilly Destinations Are Currently Closed?

The August 1 Kerala Tourism advisory was broad in scope. Under its terms, all tourist spots in districts under Red and Orange alerts are off-limits until the weather warnings are lifted. As of Sunday evening, the districts under Red alert were Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasaragod. Ernakulam, Thrissur, and Palakkad were on Orange Alert.

Specific formally closed sites named by authorities include all high-range Palakkad tourist destinations — among them Nelliyampathy hill station and Malampuzha. Kottayam's Ilaveezhapoonchira, Illikkalkallu, and Marmala waterfalls were also shut. Ponmudi eco-tourism center in Thiruvananthapuram was closed. Night travel to Thrissur's hilly areas was banned from 7 PM to 6 AM, and trekking and wilderness camping in Thrissur's forest zones were suspended. All tourist spots under the Ernakulam DTPC were shut.

Travelers planning to visit any Kerala destination in or adjacent to the Western Ghats in the coming days should check directly with the relevant district collector's office or the Kerala Tourism official website before departing, as closure orders extend automatically until weather warnings are withdrawn and can be re-imposed. The State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) indicated as of August 2 that while rainfall intensity was easing, a re-intensification was expected around August 7.

Is It Safe to Visit Kerala Waterfalls in Monsoon Season?

The appeal is real: Kerala's waterfalls are at their most powerful and visually dramatic during the southwest monsoon (June through September), drawing visitors from across southern India and internationally. But the conditions that create that spectacle also make the sites acutely dangerous. A waterfall like Palakkuzhi, situated deep inside forested terrain without managed access infrastructure, can experience sudden and dramatic surge events when upstream rainfall flows into a narrow catchment and discharges in a concentrated rush — with no visible warning at the base level where visitors stand.

The deaths at Palakkuzhi fit a pattern that Kerala authorities and safety advocates have flagged throughout the 2026 monsoon season. The Goa Chronicle, surveying India's waterfall fatalities in the first half of 2026, noted that deaths repeatedly occurred in zones where public access had already been prohibited, and that "enforcement proved insufficient to prevent the loss of life." The 2024 Bhushi Dam waterfall deaths near Lonavala, Maharashtra — in which five people, most of them children, were killed after entering a restricted zone — established the same template: a warning exists, no physical barrier exists, people enter, people die.

For Kerala specifically, the practical implication is that a district administration or tourism authority announcement that a site is "restricted" or "closed" does not guarantee that the access road or trail to that site is physically blocked. As Palakkuzhi demonstrated on August 2, it may mean only that a legal order exists — one that a visiting group from another state, unfamiliar with local weather conditions or local media coverage, may never have seen.

The safest approach for any traveler planning a Kerala waterfall visit between now and mid-September is to check the current IMD district alert level before traveling, and to treat any Orange or Red alert designation as a hard stop. Travelers already in Kerala who encounter a warning sign, a notice of restriction, or advice from local residents not to proceed should treat that as equivalent to a physical barrier — because, as Sunday's events showed, an official ban does not always come with one.

Bhanupriya's body was expected to be released to her family following postmortem on Monday, according to police. The police investigation into how the group entered the restricted area remains open.

Weather Update Today के मुताबिक दिल्ली, नोएडा, गाजियाबाद, गुरुग्राम और फरीदाबाद में 5 अगस्त तक मौसम सुहावना लेकिन अस्थिर बना रहेगा। आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे और कई इलाकों में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश होने की संभावना है। सुबह और दोपहर के समय बारिश के साथ तेज हवाएं भी चल सकती हैं, जिनकी रफ्तार करीब 30 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा रहने का अनुमान है।

उत्तर प्रदेश में कई जिलों के लिए भारी बारिश का अलर्ट

जम्मू-कश्मीर और हिमाचल प्रदेश में मौसम रहेगा चुनौतीपूर्ण

Weather Update Today मौसम विभाग के अनुसार जम्मू-कश्मीर में 3 से 6 अगस्त तक कई स्थानों पर भारी बारिश के साथ गरज-चमक और तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं। वहीं हिमाचल प्रदेश के चंबा, कांगड़ा, कुल्लू, मंडी, शिमला, किन्नौर, हमीरपुर और लाहौल-स्पीति समेत कई जिलों में 8 अगस्त तक भारी बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। कुछ इलाकों में हवा की गति 50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है, जिससे भूस्खलन और सड़क बाधित होने की आशंका भी बनी रहेगी।

Weather Update Today के मुताबिक महाराष्ट्र के कई जिलों में 3 से 8 अगस्त तक ऑरेंज और येलो अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। रत्नागिरी, सतारा, नागपुर, अकोला, अमरावती, बुलढाणा, यवतमाल, वर्धा, भंडारा, गोंदिया, चंद्रपुर और गढ़चिरौली में गरज-चमक के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना है। पंजाब में 3 से 6 अगस्त तक कई स्थानों पर बारिश का दौर जारी रहेगा, जबकि झारखंड में 3 से 8 अगस्त तक लगातार बारिश और तेज हवाओं का असर देखने को मिल सकता है।

पूर्वोत्तर भारत में मानसून अगले पांच दिनों तक और मजबूत रहने वाला है। अरुणाचल प्रदेश, असम, मेघालय, नागालैंड, मणिपुर, मिजोरम और त्रिपुरा में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश की संभावना जताई गई है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार कुछ क्षेत्रों में बिजली गिरने और तेज हवाएं चलने की भी आशंका है, इसलिए लोगों को विशेष सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी गई है।

राजस्थान और आसपास बने निम्न दबाव क्षेत्र का असर उत्तर भारत के कई राज्यों में दिखाई देगा। हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़, उत्तराखंड और राजस्थान के कई जिलों में अगले कुछ दिनों तक बारिश, गरज-चमक और तेज हवाओं की संभावना बनी हुई है। पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में लोगों को विशेष सावधानी बरतने की सलाह दी गई है।

मॉनसून ट्रफ और पश्चिमी विक्षोभ से बढ़ेगी बारिश

title: পাঁচদিন ভারী বৃষ্টির আভাস, তৈরি হতে পারে সাময়িক বন্যার ঝুঁকি - Kaler Alo
article_text:
দেশজুড়ে আবারও আবহাওয়ার বড় ধরনের পরিবর্তনের আভাস পাওয়া গেছে। ৩ আগস্ট থেকে শুরু হয়ে ৮ আগস্ট পর্যন্ত দেশের বিভিন্ন অঞ্চলে সক্রিয় থাকতে পারে আংশিক বৃষ্টি বলয়। এ সময়ে দেশের প্রায় ৫০ থেকে ৬০ শতাংশ এলাকায় কমবেশি উল্লেখযোগ্য বৃষ্টিপাত হতে পারে।
তবে এটি আংশিক বৃষ্টি বলয় হওয়ায় সব জায়গায় সমান বর্ষণ না হয়ে নির্দিষ্ট কিছু অঞ্চলে অতিভারী বৃষ্টি হতে পারে বলে জানিয়েছে বেসরকারি আবহাওয়া পর্যবেক্ষণ সংস্থা বাংলাদেশ ওয়েদার অবজারভেশন টিম (বিডব্লিউওটি)।
বিডব্লিউওটি জানায়, বৃষ্টি বলয়টি চলাকালীন রংপুর, রাজশাহী, ময়মনসিংহ ও সিলেট বিভাগে সর্বোচ্চ সক্রিয়তা দেখা যেতে পারে। পাশাপাশি খুলনা, ঢাকা, বরিশাল ও চট্টগ্রাম বিভাগে মাঝারি ধরনের সক্রিয় থাকার সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে।
বৃষ্টি বলয়টি শুরুতে রংপুর, ময়মনসিংহ ও সিলেট বিভাগে সক্রিয় হয়ে ৪ আগস্ট রাজশাহীতে এবং ৫ ও ৬ আগস্ট দেশের অধিকাংশ এলাকায় ব্যাপকভাবে ছড়িয়ে পড়তে পারে। ৫ ও ৬ আগস্ট পুরো দেশেই বৃষ্টিপাতের তীব্রতা সবচেয়ে বেশি থাকার সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে।
সংস্থাটি জানায়, এ বৃষ্টি বলয়ের প্রভাবে উত্তরাঞ্চল ও উত্তর-পূর্বাঞ্চলের নদ-নদীর পানি দ্রুত বৃদ্ধি পাওয়ার আশঙ্কা রয়েছে। ফলে রংপুর, রাজশাহী, ময়মনসিংহ ও সিলেট বিভাগের নিচু ও অতিবন্যাপ্রবণ এলাকাগুলোতে সাময়িক বন্যার ঝুঁকি তৈরি হতে পারে।
একই সময়ে এসব অঞ্চলে রোদের উপস্থিতি খুবই কম থাকবে এবং সার্বিকভাবে ৫ ও ৬ আগস্ট সারা দেশের আকাশ মেঘলা থাকার সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে। যদিও খুলনা, বরিশাল ও চট্টগ্রাম বিভাগের দক্ষিণাঞ্চলে মাঝে মাঝে রোদের দেখা মিলতে পারে।
বিভাগভিত্তিক গড় বৃষ্টিপাতের পরিসংখ্যান দিয়ে বিডব্লিউওটি জানায়, রংপুর বিভাগে সবচেয়ে বেশি ২২০ থেকে ২৫০ মিলিমিটার বৃষ্টিপাত হতে পারে। এছাড়া সিলেট ও ময়মনসিংহ বিভাগে ২০০ থেকে ২৫০ মিলিমিটার এবং রাজশাহী বিভাগে ১৭০ থেকে ২২০ মিলিমিটার বৃষ্টির সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে।
অন্যদিকে খুলনা বিভাগে ১৪০ থেকে ১৫০ মিলিমিটার, ঢাকা বিভাগে ১০০ থেকে ১২০ মিলিমিটার এবং চট্টগ্রাম ও বরিশাল বিভাগে ৮০ থেকে ১২০ মিলিমিটার পর্যন্ত বৃষ্টি হতে পারে, যা সাধারণত ৩ থেকে ৪ দিনের মধ্যে সম্পন্ন হতে পারে। তবে এই পরিসংখ্যান বিভাগীয় গড় ধারণা মাত্র, জেলা পর্যায়ে কিছুটা কম-বেশি হতে পারে।
সমুদ্রের পরিস্থিতির বিষয়ে তারা জানায়, এ সময়ে সাগরে কোনো বড় ধরনের সিস্টেম তৈরির সম্ভাবনা কম থাকলেও সঞ্চালনশীল গভীর মেঘমালার কারণে হঠাৎ দমকা বা ঝড়ো হাওয়া বয়ে যেতে পারে। তাই সাগর ও উপকূলীয় এলাকায় চলাচলের ক্ষেত্রে বিশেষ সতর্কতা অবলম্বনের পরামর্শ দেওয়া হয়েছে।
প্রাকৃতিক নিয়মে বায়ুমণ্ডলের পরিবর্তনের কারণে এ বৃষ্টি বলয়ের সময়সূচি ও শক্তিতে কিছুটা হ্রাস-বৃদ্ধি বা পরিবর্তন আসতে পারে বলেও উল্লেখ করা হয়।

ગુજરાતમાં આજે ક્યાં પડશે વરસાદ? જાણો ચોમાસું ક્યાં પહોંચ્યું
2026-06-11 08:28:00
Author: Mayur Patel

Ai Image




અમદાવાદ-નવી દિલ્હીઃ હવામાન વિભાગ અનુસાર વેસ્ટર્ન ડિસ્ટર્બન્સના કારણે ઉત્તર પશ્ચિમ ભારતમાં 13 તારીખ સુધી વરસાદનો પ્રભાવ જોવા મળશે. ગાજવીજ સાથે ભારે પવન અને કરા પણ પડશે. ઉત્તર પૂર્વના રાજ્યો તથા પશ્ચિમ બંગાળમાં આગામી પાંચથી સાત દિવસ એક બે સ્થળોએ 7 થી લઈ 20 સેમી સુધી વરસાદ પડી શકે છે. દક્ષિણ ભારતના કેરળ, કર્ણાટક, તમિલનાડુમાં ભારે વરસાદનું પૂર્વાનુમાન છે. ગુજરાતમાં ચોમાસાના આગમન પહેલા મોટા ભાગના વિસ્તારમાં વાદળછાયું વાતાવરણ જોવા મળી રહ્યું છે. દક્ષિણ ગુજરાતમાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ  હળવા વરસાદી ઝાપટાં પડી રહ્યા છે.

 

ગુજરાતમાં કેવું રહેશે હવામાન

 

આજે સુરત સહિત દક્ષિણ ગુજરાતમાં પવન સાથે વરસાદની શક્યતા વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે. 16 જૂન સુધી દક્ષિણ ગુજરાત, સૌરાષ્ટ્ર અને મધ્ય ગુજરાતમાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ હળવાથી મધ્યમ વરસાદની શક્યતા છે. નૈઋત્યનું ચોમાસું ગુજરાત તરફ ધીમે ધીમે આગળ વધી રહ્યું છે, જેના પગલે સક્રિય થયેલી વરસાદી સિસ્ટમ રાજ્યના વિવિધ ભાગોમાં જોવા મળી શકે છે. 12 થી 16 જૂન દરમિયાન દક્ષિણ ગુજરાત, મધ્ય ગુજરાત અને સૌરાષ્ટ્રમાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ હળવોથી મધ્યમ વરસાદ વરસી શકે છે. અમદાવાદમાં આજે મહત્તમ તાપમાન 42 ડિગ્રી આસપાસ રહી શકે છે. લોકોને કાળઝાળ ગરમી અને બફારાનો અનુભવ થશે.

 

ચોમાસું ક્યાં પહોંચ્યું?

 

ચોમાસું આગામી ત્રણથી ચાર દિવસમાં મહારાષ્ટ્ર, કર્ણાટક, તેલંગાણા, આંધ્રપ્રદેશમાં આગળ વધી શકે છે અને તમિલનાડુના બાકીના ભાગોને પણ આવરી શકે છે. આ દરમિયાન છત્તીસગઢ, બિહાર, ઝારખંડ, ઓડિશાના કેટલાક ભાગોમાં ચોમાસું દસ્તક આપી શકે છે. ચોમાસાને આગળ વધવા માટે સાનુકૂળ પરિસ્થિતિઓ છે. વેસ્ટર્ન ડિસ્ટર્બન્સના કારણે મધ્ય ભાગમાં લો પ્રેશર સર્જાયું છે. આ કારણે ઉત્તર-પશ્ચિમ ભારતમાં આગામી 24 કલાકમાં તાપમાનમાં કોઈ મોટો ફેરફાર જોવા નહીં મળે. ત્યારબાદ 13 તારીખ સુધી પારો 3 થી 5 ડિગ્રી સેલ્સિયસ સુધી ગગડી શકે છે. જે પછી તાપમાન ફરીથી 2 થી 4 ડિગ્રી સુધી વધી શકે છે. દેશના મધ્ય ભાગમાં આગામી 3 દિવસ એટલે કે 12 તારીખ સુધી તાપમાનમાં બહુ ફેરફાર જોવા નહીં મળે, પરંતુ ત્યારબાદ તાપમાનમાં 2 થી 3 ડિગ્રી સુધીનો ઘટાડો જોવા મળી શકે છે. પૂર્વ ભારતમાં 2 દિવસ સુધી તાપમાનમાં ખાસ ફેરફાર નહીં થાય. ત્યારબાદ 12 થી 14 તારીખ વચ્ચે તાપમાનમાં 2 થી 4 ડિગ્રી સુધીનો ઘટાડો થઈ શકે છે.

 

 

 

મધ્યપ્રદેશ-બિહારમાં ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ

 

પૂર્વી મધ્યપ્રદેશ, ઝારખંડ, ઓડિશા અને બિહાર, પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ, આસામ, મેઘાલયમાં ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું છે. આ સાથે અંદામાન અને નિકોબાર ટાપુઓમાં પણ ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ અપાયું છે. ગાજવીજ સાથે વીજળી અને તેજ પવનની અસર જોવા મળશે. આસામ, મેઘાલય, પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ અને સિક્કિમમાં એક કે બે સ્થળોએ ભારે વરસાદ પડી શકે છે. ભારે વરસાદની અસર અરૂણાચલ પ્રદેશ, નાગાલેન્ડ, મણિપુર, ત્રિપુરા, તેલંગાણા, કર્ણાટક, દક્ષિણ કોંકણ, દરિયાકાંઠાના કર્ણાટક, કેરળ, તમિલનાડુ અને લક્ષદ્વીપમાં જોવા મળશે. કર્ણાટક, ગોવા, કેરળમાં 30 થી 40 કિમીની ઝડપે પવન ફૂંકાઈ શકે છે.

 

યુપી-કાશ્મીરમાં હીટવેવનો પ્રકોપ યથાવત રહેશે

 

જમ્મુ-કાશ્મીર, હિમાચલ પ્રદેશ, ઉત્તર પ્રદેશ, પંજાબ, હરિયાણા, રાજસ્થાનમાં હીટવેવનો પ્રકોપ ચાલુ રહેશે. વેસ્ટર્ન ડિસ્ટર્બન્સના કારણે જમ્મુ-કાશ્મીર, પંજાબ, હરિયાણા, ઉત્તર પ્રદેશ અને ઉત્તરાખંડમાં કરા પડી શકે છે. આ તમામ સ્થળોએ ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું છે. રાજસ્થાન અને ઉત્તર પ્રદેશમાં એક-બે સ્થળોએ ધૂળની ડમરીઓ સાથે આંધી આવવાની સંભાવના છે. પૂર્વ ભારતમાં ભારે પવન અને ગાજવીજ સાથે વીજળીનો પ્રભાવ જોવા મળી શકે છે.

હવામાન વિભાગે ગુજરાત માટે આજે વરસાદને લઈને મહત્વની આગાહી જાહેર કરી છે. વિભાગના જણાવ્યા મુજબ આજે મધ્ય ગુજરાત અને દક્ષિણ ગુજરાતના વિસ્તારોમાં સામાન્ય વરસાદની શક્યતા છે. બીજી તરફ ઉત્તર ગુજરાતના અનેક વિસ્તારોમાં ભારેથી અતિ ભારે વરસાદ વરસી શકે છે તેવી આગાહી કરવામાં આવી છે. વરસાદી માહોલને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને લોકોને સાવચેતી રાખવા અને જરૂર વગર બહાર ન નીકળવાની સલાહ આપવામાં આવી છે. નીચાણવાળા વિસ્તારોમાં પાણી ભરાવાની સ્થિતિ સર્જાઈ શકે છે, તેથી સ્થાનિક તંત્ર પણ સતર્ક બન્યું છે.
ઉત્તર ગુજરાતમાં ભારેથી અતિ ભારે વરસાદની આગાહીને કારણે ખેડૂતો અને સામાન્ય નાગરિકોને ખાસ સાવચેતી રાખવાની અપીલ કરવામાં આવી છે. ભારે વરસાદ દરમિયાન નદી-નાળા અને નીચાણવાળા વિસ્તારોમાં જવાનું ટાળવાની સલાહ આપવામાં આવી છે. હવામાન વિભાગ સતત સ્થિતિ પર નજર રાખી રહ્યું છે અને જરૂરિયાત મુજબ આગામી અપડેટ પણ જાહેર કરવામાં આવશે.
સૌરાષ્ટ્રના દરિયાકાંઠાના વિસ્તારો માટે પણ મહત્વની આગાહી કરવામાં આવી છે. ખાસ કરીને દ્વારકા અને જામનગર જિલ્લામાં ભારે વરસાદ પડવાની સંભાવના વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે. આ બંને જિલ્લામાં વરસાદી માહોલ વધુ તીવ્ર બની શકે છે. ભારે વરસાદને કારણે કેટલીક જગ્યાએ પાણી ભરાવા, ટ્રાફિક પર અસર અને જનજીવન પ્રભાવિત થવાની શક્યતા પણ વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે.
દરિયાકાંઠાના વિસ્તારોમાં ખરાબ હવામાનને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને હવામાન વિભાગે માછીમારોને ખાસ સૂચના આપી છે. આગામી દિવસોમાં દરિયામાં પવનની ગતિ અને દરિયાની સ્થિતિ જોખમી બની શકે છે. તેથી માછીમારોને દરિયો ન ખેડવાની સ્પષ્ટ સલાહ આપવામાં આવી છે. જે માછીમારો દરિયામાં ગયા હોય તેમને પણ શક્ય તેટલી વહેલી તકે પરત ફરી આવવા માટે સૂચના આપવામાં આવી છે.
અમદાવાદ શહેર માટે હવામાન વિભાગે રાહતના સમાચાર આપ્યા છે. આગાહી મુજબ અમદાવાદમાં આગામી ત્રણ દિવસ દરમિયાન ઓછો વરસાદ રહેવાની શક્યતા છે. શહેરમાં ભારે વરસાદની શક્યતા ઓછી હોવાનું જણાવવામાં આવ્યું છે, જોકે વાદળછાયું વાતાવરણ અને છૂટાછવાયા હળવા ઝાપટાં પડી શકે છે. તેથી લોકોને હવામાન વિભાગની આગામી આગાહીઓ પર નજર રાખવાની સલાહ આપવામાં આવી છે.
ગુજરાતમાં ચોમાસાની સ્થિતિને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને હવામાન વિભાગ સતત જિલ્લાવાર આગાહીઓ જાહેર કરી રહ્યું છે. આજે મધ્ય ગુજરાત અને દક્ષિણ ગુજરાતમાં સામાન્ય વરસાદ, ઉત્તર ગુજરાતમાં ભારેથી અતિ ભારે વરસાદ તેમજ સૌરાષ્ટ્રના દ્વારકા અને જામનગરમાં ભારે વરસાદની આગાહી કરવામાં આવી છે. સાથે જ માછીમારોને દરિયો ન ખેડવાની સૂચના આપવામાં આવી છે, જ્યારે અમદાવાદમાં આગામી ત્રણ દિવસ વરસાદનું પ્રમાણ ઓછું રહેવાની શક્યતા વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે. તેથી તમામ નાગરિકોને હવામાન વિભાગની સૂચનાઓનું પાલન કરવા અને જરૂરી સાવચેતી રાખવા અપીલ કરવામાં આવી છે.

title: Assam Floods Displace 2 Lakh: Monsoon Fury Continues, IMD Alert - Prag News
article_text:
The ongoing monsoon season continues to wreak havoc across India, with Assam experiencing particularly severe devastation as floodwaters displace nearly 1.92 lakh residents. Five districts in the state—Sivasagar, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, and Charaideo—are bearing the brunt of the deluge, where 379 villages have been submerged and thousands of hectares of agricultural land destroyed.
As rivers swell dangerously, state authorities are working tirelessly, conducting round-the-clock monitoring and deploying relief and rehabilitation operations to assist affected communities. Despite the challenging circumstances, stories of extraordinary human resilience have emerged from the hardest-hit areas.
In Sivasagar's Nepali Khuti, for instance, six local villagers exemplified courage by using country-made wooden boats to rescue over 1,000 people. These individuals were trapped across five flood-affected villages after water levels surged unexpectedly. One of the rescuers, Chouhan Choudhury, recounted the harrowing experience, stating, "We had never seen water rise like this. We rescued everyone we could using our boats," detailing how families stranded on rooftops, elevated platforms, and even trees were safely evacuated.
Amidst the widespread emergency, state Minister Pijush Hazarika has reviewed relief operations in Demow and Nazira, underscoring the government's commitment to supporting those impacted. As the monsoon progresses, authorities remain vigilant, coordinating efforts to mitigate further damage and provide essential aid to the displaced population.

title: Monsoon Havoc Across India: Nearly 2 Lakh Displaced in Assam as Floods, Flash Floods Batter Multiple States - Open Magazine
article_text:
The monsoon's destructive march across India is showing little sign of slowing. Floods, flash floods and relentless rainfall have disrupted life across several states, but Assam continues to bear the brunt, with nearly 1.92 lakh people displaced across five districts as rivers remain swollen and villages stay submerged.
The worst-affected districts in Assam include Sivasagar, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Charaideo, where 379 villages have been inundated and thousands of hectares of farmland damaged. Relief and rehabilitation operations are continuing, with state authorities monitoring the situation round the clock.
Amid the devastation, stories of extraordinary resilience have emerged. In Sivasagar's Nepali Khuti, six villagers used country-made wooden boats to rescue more than 1,000 people trapped across five flood-hit villages after water levels rose with alarming speed.
"We had never seen water rise like this. We rescued everyone we could using our boats," said rescuer Chouhan Choudhury, recalling how families stranded on rooftops, raised platforms and trees were ferried to safety.

Assam Minister Pijush Hazarika reviewed relief operations in Demow and Nazira, while Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma acknowledged contributions of ₹11 crore from Gautam Adani and ₹21 crore from Reliance Foundation to the state's relief fund.
While Assam remains the epicentre, heavy monsoon rains have triggered emergencies across several other states.
In Kerala, overflowing rivers and incessant rain have forced 5,792 people into 209 relief camps, damaged homes and inundated markets. In Ranni town, traders watched helplessly as the Pamba River overflowed, causing losses worth lakhs of rupees.
In Chhattisgarh, intense rainfall resembling a cloudburst devastated the Abujhmad region in Narayanpur district. More than 50 houses were damaged, with residents describing the flooding as unprecedented after entire settlements were washed away.
Gujarat remains on alert after the IMD issued red warnings for heavy to very heavy rainfall across several districts, including Ahmedabad, Rajkot, Morbi and Surendranagar, while widespread waterlogging has been reported across Saurashtra.
Authorities are also monitoring flood-like conditions in Odisha, while Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand remain on alert over rising river levels and the risk of flash floods.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned that rainfall is likely to intensify over Northeast India and the Himalayan foothills over the next four to five days, with flash flood risks continuing in parts of Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Kerala and Karnataka.
Meanwhile, the Centre has stepped up assistance for flood-hit states. Union Home Minister Amit Shah approved fresh financial aid, including ₹379.35 crore for Assam, while additional assistance has been sanctioned for Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha, Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.
With more rain forecast in the days ahead, authorities have urged residents in vulnerable areas to remain vigilant as India's annual monsoon continues to test lives, infrastructure and disaster response systems.

title: Karnataka farmers seek drought relief as sugarcane crop suffers from monsoon deficit - ChiniMandi
article_text:
Dharwad: Farmer organisations in Karnataka have urged the state government to declare the state drought-affected after deficient southwest monsoon rainfall damaged sugarcane and other crops, raising concerns over farm incomes and the upcoming crushing season.

Protests led by Karnataka Hasiru Sene, Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and AIKKMS have intensified in Dharwad district, where farmers said sugarcane fields, particularly in Kalaghatagi taluk, have suffered significant damage due to prolonged dry weather. The organisations demanded that sugarcane be included under the state’s crop compensation scheme and called for waiver of crop loans taken from nationalised, cooperative and private banks, Deccan Herald reported.

Farmer groups said repeated drought-like conditions over the past five years have weakened the agricultural sector and urged the government to provide immediate relief to affected growers.

Dharwad Deputy Commissioner Snehal R said the district has received 178 mm of rainfall against the normal 275 mm, recording a 35% rainfall deficit during the southwest monsoon season. Rainfall over the past week stood at just 0.9 mm, compared with the normal 37 mm, resulting in a 76% weekly deficit.

According to the administration, seven of Dharwad’s eight taluks have received below-normal rainfall, with only Kundgol recording excess rainfall. Moisture stress has affected standing crops, while drinking water shortages have emerged in 18 villages across three taluks.

Besides sugarcane, onion and chilli crops have also been damaged by inadequate rainfall. However, farmer organisations stressed that sugarcane growers should receive compensation as the crop is not currently covered under the compensation scheme.

A delegation of farmers also urged the Karnataka government to declare the entire state drought-affected, conduct an immediate crop damage survey and provide ₹50,000 per hectare as crop loss compensation before September 15 to help farmers prepare for the rabi season.

जागरण टीम, कुल्लू/शिमला। हिमाचल प्रदेश में मूसलाधार बारिश ने कुल्लू जिले के निरमंड क्षेत्र में भारी तबाही मचाई है। फ्लैश फ्लड और भूस्खलन से एक स्कूल भवन ध्वस्त हो गया है। इसके अलावा अन्य भवन भी क्षतिग्रस्त हुए हैं। बाढ़ से सेब के 500 से ज्यादा पौधे तबाह हो गए हैं। लोग घर छोड़कर सुरक्षित स्थान की ओर भाग गए। कई लोगों ने सड़क किनारे खड़ी गाड़ियों में रात बिताई।

स्कूल भवन ध्वस्त

पंचायत बारी के पांकवा गांव में वर्ष 1993 में निर्मित सरकारी प्राइमरी स्कूल भवन ध्वस्त हो गया। पहाड़ी से भारी मात्रा में मलबा स्कूल भवन पर आ गिरा, जिससे भवन उपयोग के लायक नहीं रहा। राहत की बात यह रही कि हादसा रात के समय हुआ, इसलिए कोई जनहानि नहीं हुई।

सेब के पौधे नष्ट, गोशालाएं भी क्षतिग्रस्त

करीब 500 से अधिक सेब के पौधे नष्ट हो गए हैं, जबकि कई गोशालाएं भी क्षतिग्रस्त हुई हैं। प्रभावित परिवारों को लाखों रुपये के नुकसान का अनुमान लगाया जा रहा है। प्रारंभिक आकलन के अनुसार लक्ष्मण राठौर, महेश्वर सिंह ठाकुर, हिमेश अजेय, श्याम सिंह, सेस राम और सोहन लाल सहित कई बागवानों के बगीचों को भारी नुकसान पहुंचा है। 

मकान भी खतरे में

लगातार हो रहे भूस्खलन से सेस राम का मकान भी खतरे की जद में आ गया है। एहतियात के तौर पर परिवार को मकान खाली कर सुरक्षित स्थान पर पहुंचाया जा रहा है।

स्कूल में बच्चों का रिकॉर्ड भी दफन

विद्यालय के भीतर बच्चों का शैक्षणिक रिकॉर्ड, महत्वपूर्ण दस्तावेज और अन्य सामग्री मलबे में दब गई है। बचा हुआ भवन कभी भी गिर सकता है, इसलिए बाकी रिकॉर्ड को बाहर निकालना भी जोखिम भरा हो गया है। ग्रामीणों ने प्रशासन से तत्काल निरीक्षण कर बच्चों की पढ़ाई के लिए वैकल्पिक व्यवस्था करने और रिकॉर्ड सुरक्षित निकालने की मांग की है।

टिकरी कैंची में आई बाढ़

उधर, टिकरी कैंची नाले में जलस्तर अचानक बढ़ने से आसपास के गांवों के लोग पूरी रात दहशत में रहे। कई परिवारों ने पूरी रात जागकर बिताई, जबकि कुछ लोगों ने सुरक्षा के लिए रात वाहन में गुजारी। वहीं छोए-छोए नाले ने भी रौद्र रूप दिखाया, जिससे आसपास के क्षेत्रों में भय का माहौल बना रहा।

ठियोग में पहाड़ी से कार पर गिरा मलबा

वहीं, जिला शिमला के ठियोग क्षेत्र में प्रेमघाट बाईपास सड़क पर एक कार पहाड़ी से गिरे मलबे की चपेट में आ गई। एचपी 23 डी-7742 दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हो गई। घटना में वाहन को भारी क्षति पहुंची है। घटना के समय वाहन में किसी व्यक्ति के होने संबंधी कोई सूचना प्राप्त नहीं हुई है।

सातारा, रायगड, पुणे आणि कोल्हापूर घाटमाथ्यावर जोरदार पाऊस होईल. भंडारा, गोदिंया, वर्धा, अकोला, गडचिरोली या जिल्ह्यांमध्ये विजांच्या कडकडाटासह पाऊस होईल. आज मुंबईमध्येही पावसाचा इशारा देण्यात आला असून पावसाचा अलर्ट जारी करण्यात आला. मराठवाड्यातील काही भागात जोरदार पाऊस हजेरी लावेल.  (Weather Update)

Pune: Villages in Maharashtra’s Satara district continue to face severe transport disruptions during the monsoon, with damaged roads, overflowing streams and limited public transport leaving several settlements temporarily isolated. The recurring connectivity crisis highlights the urgent need for climate resilient roads that can withstand extreme rainfall while ensuring uninterrupted access to education, healthcare and essential public services.
In villages such as Navaja and Patherpunj, persistent rainfall has once again exposed the vulnerability of rural infrastructure. Heavy precipitation has damaged key approach roads, disrupting Maharashtra State Road Transport bus operations and forcing residents to depend on a limited number of private vehicles. In some areas, commuters must cross waterlogged stretches on unpaved roads, making travel both expensive and hazardous during the peak monsoon season. Agriculture department rainfall records indicate that parts of Satara witnessed exceptionally heavy rainfall during the last week of July, intensifying pressure on already fragile transport infrastructure. Experts say such weather events are becoming more frequent, reinforcing concerns that conventional road construction methods are no longer adequate for regions experiencing prolonged high-intensity rainfall.
The absence of reliable all-weather connectivity has affected daily life across these villages. Schoolchildren travelling to neighbouring towns for secondary education must rely on overcrowded shared vehicles operating at fixed hours, while residents requiring healthcare, banking and government services face long delays. Local governance specialists argue that inadequate rural mobility not only affects quality of life but also widens regional development disparities. The challenge extends beyond transportation. In elevated settlements such as Patherpunj, overflowing seasonal streams regularly submerge approach roads, restricting access for standard vehicles and increasing travel costs for residents who must hire larger utility vehicles. Emergency response also becomes difficult because telecommunications coverage remains limited in several remote locations, reducing the ability of residents to seek assistance during extreme weather events. Urban and rural infrastructure planners believe climate resilient roads should become a priority under state infrastructure programmes. Elevated road sections, improved drainage systems, stronger retaining walls, flood-resistant culverts and slope stabilisation measures can significantly improve year-round connectivity while reducing recurring maintenance costs. Such investments are increasingly viewed as essential adaptation measures in districts experiencing changing monsoon patterns linked to climate variability.
The recurring disruptions also raise broader questions about balanced regional development. While Maharashtra continues investing in urban transport corridors and expressways, experts suggest that resilient rural infrastructure deserves equal attention because it supports education, healthcare access, agricultural markets and local economic activity. Reliable road connectivity remains fundamental to preventing migration driven by inadequate public services. As another monsoon season exposes longstanding infrastructure gaps, planners are expected to review engineering standards for vulnerable hill roads and remote settlements. Strengthening climate resilient roads alongside improved digital connectivity and emergency services could help ensure that communities remain connected throughout the year despite increasingly unpredictable weather conditions.

Bihar Weather Update: पटना समेत 16 जिलों में मूसलाधार बारिश से सुहाना हुआ मौसम, पांच जिलों में भारी वर्षा का अलर्ट
BY PRABHAT RANJAN
EDITED BY: NISHANT BHARTI
UPDATED: MON, 03 AUG 2026 07:28 AM (IST)

पटना समेत बिहार के 16 जिलों में मानसून की झमाझम बारिश से मौसम सुहाना हो गया है और लोगों को गर्मी से राहत मिली है। ...और पढ़ें

बिहार का मौसम ( एआई जेनरेटेड तस्वीर )

HIGHLIGHTS

पटना सहित 16 जिलों में हुई झमाझम बारिश।

पांच जिलों में भारी से अति भारी वर्षा का अलर्ट।

उमस भरी गर्मी से लोगों को मिली बड़ी राहत।

जागरण संवाददाता, पटना। प्रदेश में मानसून की गतिविधियां बने होने के कारण पटना सहित 16 जिलों में सावन का बदरा झूम कर बरस रहा है। रविवार को सुबह से छाए काले घने बादलों के बाद तेज वर्षा से मौसम पूरी तरह सुहाना बना हुआ है। वर्षा के कारण लोगों को उमस भरी गर्मी से राहत मिली है। 

मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र पटना के अनुसार अगले 24 घंटे के दौरान पटना सहित शेष जिलों में बादलों की आवाजाही बने होने के साथ कई स्थानों पर रिमझिम वर्षा की संभावना है। जबकि, राज्य के पांच जिलों में भारी व अति भारी वर्षा को लेकर चेतावनी जारी की गई है। 

विज्ञापन हटाएं
सिर्फ खबर पढ़ें
5 जिलों में भारी बारिश की चेतावनी

गोपालगंज एवं सिवान में अति भारी एवं किशनगंज, सुपौल एवं पश्चिमी चंपारण में भारी वर्षा को लेकर चेतावनी जारी की गई है। अगले तीन से चार दिनों के दौरान प्रदेश के अलग-अलग भागों में वर्षा की गतिविधियां बने होने के साथ 30-40 किमी प्रतिघंटा की रफ्तार से हवा चलने की संभावना है। दो दिनों के बाद अधिकतम तापमान में दो से तीन डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट का पूर्वानुमान है। 

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार चार अगस्त को उत्तर पश्चिम भारत में नया पश्चिमी विक्षोभ बनने की संभावना है। इसके कारण प्रदेश के अलग-अलग भागों में वर्षा की गतिविधियां बने रहने के आसार है। रविवार को राजधानी सहित भागलपुर, सबौर, वाल्मीकि नगर, छपरा, मुजफ्फरपुर, सुपौल, डेहरी, मधेपुरा, जहानाबाद आदि जगहों पर बदरा खूब बरसा। 

राजधानी में 5.4 मिमी वर्षा दर्ज 

राजधानी में 5.4 मिमी वर्षा दर्ज की गई। बीते 24 घंटे के दौरान रोहतास के कोचस में 80 मिमी सर्वाधिक वर्षा दर्ज की गई। वर्षा के कारण पटना सहित ज्यादातर जिलों के तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गई। 

पटना का अधिकतम तापमान 34.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस एवं 36.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस के साथ कैमूर में सर्वाधिक तापमान दर्ज किया गया। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार प्रदेश में अभी भी सामान्य से 43 प्रतिशत कम वर्षा की स्थिति बनी हुई है।

प्रमुख शहरों में दर्ज हुई वर्षा

पश्चिम चंपारण के चनपटिया में 62.2 मिमी, नरकटियागंज में 62.2 मिमी, नंदनगढ़ में 59 मिमी, शेखपुरा के घाट कुसुंबा में 51 मिमी, सुपौल के पिपरा में 50 मिमी, किशनगंज के तैयबपुर में 46.8 मिमी, सिवान के बसंतपुर में 46 मिमी दर्ज की गई।

कटिहार के बरारी में 44 मिमी, मधुबनी के लौकाही में 41 मिमी, सुपौल के बसुआ में 40.6 मिमी, रोहतास के बिक्रमगंज में 39 मिमी, शेखपुरा में 38 मिमी, सुपौल के किशनपुर में 38 मिमी, पश्चिम चंपारण के वाल्मीकि नगर में 37.8 मिमी, भोजपुर के पीरो में 28 मिमी, पश्चिम चंपारण के सिकटा में 27 मिमी दर्ज की गई।

title: Heavy rain likely in eight Tamil Nadu districts today; cloudy sky, light showers in Chennai - DD News
article_text:
Heavy rain is likely in eight districts of Tamil Nadu on Tuesday, while Chennai is expected to witness cloudy skies and light to moderate showers, according to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai.

In a statement, the weather department said an atmospheric circulation extends from the central-east Bay of Bengal to the southeast Arabian Sea, passing through the southwest Bay of Bengal, the southern Tamil Nadu coast, the Gulf of Mannar and adjoining Kanyakumari sea regions. The system is expected to influence weather conditions across several parts of the state over the coming days.

Under its impact, heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in the hilly regions of Coimbatore and Tiruppur districts, as well as in Nilgiris, Erode, Salem, Theni, Dindigul and Kanyakumari districts on Tuesday.

The department said intense spells of rain may occur in these areas and advised residents, particularly in vulnerable and hilly regions, to remain cautious as heavy showers could disrupt transportation and daily activities.

Officials added that moderate rainfall is likely at one or two places across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry from Wednesday till May 29 as the prevailing atmospheric circulation continues to influence weather patterns.

For Chennai and adjoining areas, the forecast indicates generally cloudy skies over the next 24 hours, with moderate rain and brief spells of showers likely in parts of the city.

Despite the rainfall activity, hot and humid conditions are expected to persist in Chennai, with temperatures likely to remain on the higher side. Weather experts said the combination of heat and moisture could make daytime conditions uncomfortable even during intermittent showers.

Meteorologists noted that while districts receiving substantial rainfall may experience some relief from the heat, humid conditions are expected to continue in urban centres, including Chennai. Authorities are closely monitoring the situation and may issue further advisories depending on weather developments.

title: Active Monsoon to bring heavy rain across Jharkhand till August 6 - The Jharkhand Story
article_text:
PINAKI MAJUMDAR Jamshedpur, August 3: After a prolonged spell of below-normal rainfall, Jharkhand is set to witness an active phase of the…

PINAKI MAJUMDAR

Jamshedpur, August 3: After a prolonged spell of below-normal rainfall, Jharkhand is set to witness an active phase of the southwest monsoon over the next four days, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting heavy rainfall across different parts of the state till August 6.

Advertisement

The IMD has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 40–50 kmph at isolated places across Jharkhand during the forecast period.

Heavy rain likely in phases across districts

According to the weather forecast, the focus of monsoon activity will shift to the north-western and central districts on August 4, with Hazaribagh, Koderma, Ramgarh and Bokaro likely to receive heavy rainfall.

On August 5, the rain belt is expected to move towards the south-eastern region, placing East Singhbhum, West Singhbhum and Seraikela-Kharsawan under a heavy rain alert.

Another spell of intense rainfall is likely on August 6 over Hazaribagh, Koderma, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Lohardaga, Gumla and Khunti, keeping large parts of Jharkhand under the influence of an active southwest monsoon system.

Advertisement

Weather systems driving active monsoon over Jharkhand

Meteorologists said the enhanced rainfall activity has been triggered by a favourable combination of weather systems prevailing over eastern and northwestern India.

The monsoon trough at mean sea level currently extends from Bikaner through Banasthali Vidyapeeth, Orai, Sidhi, Daltonganj and Bankura before stretching eastwards towards Manipur.

Another trough extends from west Rajasthan to Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim across a cyclonic circulation over central Rajasthan, northern Madhya Pradesh, southeast Uttar Pradesh and Bihar at an altitude of about 0.9 km above mean sea level.

Advertisement

Adding to the favourable conditions, an upper-air cyclonic circulation persists over northwest Bangladesh and adjoining Sub-Himalayan West Bengal at around 1.5 km above mean sea level. This system is continuously drawing moisture into Jharkhand and supporting widespread convective activity, leading to increased rainfall across the state.

IMD advises caution amid thunderstorms and lightning

The IMD has cautioned that thunderstorms, lightning and strong surface winds may cause localised disruptions, including damage to weak structures, uprooting of trees and temporary traffic disruptions.

Farmers have been advised to suspend agricultural operations during thunderstorms, while residents have been urged to avoid open fields, water bodies and isolated trees during lightning strikes.

Rainfall deficit likely to narrow

Despite recent showers, Jharkhand continues to face a seasonal rainfall deficit. The state has so far received 379.9 mm of rainfall against the normal 526.3 mm, leaving it with a 28 per cent deficit.

Weather experts, however, expect the widespread rainfall forecast over the next few days to significantly reduce the shortfall if it materialises. The rain is also expected to provide much-needed relief to agriculture, replenish reservoirs and groundwater levels, and improve the overall monsoon performance across Jharkhand.
